html:
In 1956 French companies found oil at Hassi Messaoud in the Sahara of Algeria, and the gas field of Hassi R'Mel the same year. Hassi Messaoud is still the country's largest oil field.

The finds came in the middle of the war of independence and made France keener to hold the Sahara. At Évian France kept rights to the oil for some years. In 1971 Algeria nationalised its oil and gas, run by Sonatrach.

Oil and gas make up nearly all of Algeria's exports and most of its state budget. They paid for free health care, schools and subsidies, but also left the country exposed to price crashes, as in 1986, which helped bring on the crisis that led to the civil war.
